author: TemplateHouse

sections.description:
TemplateHouse Block Toolkit is a powerful WordPress block library with 376+ Gutenberg blocks for building modern websites, landing pages, blogs, business websites, online stores, marketing pages, documentation, comparison pages, interactive tools, and more — directly inside the WordPress block editor.

Create professional WordPress websites without relying on Elementor, Divi, or other page builders. TemplateHouse Block Toolkit extends the native WordPress block editor with a large collection of flexible, customizable, and performance-focused blocks designed for real-world website projects.

Whether you are a blogger, marketer, business owner, freelancer, designer, developer, or agency, you can use TemplateHouse Block Toolkit to build complete page layouts and add advanced content and interactive features without writing custom code.

🔗 Free Support

376+ Powerful WordPress Blocks

TemplateHouse Block Toolkit includes 376+ Gutenberg blocks organized into 10 practical categories:

Structure – 26 Blocks
Build flexible page layouts with sections, columns, containers, headers, navigation, content layouts, and other structural elements.

Content & Typography – 38 Blocks
Improve your content with advanced headings, text styles, lists, quotes, accordions, tabs, timelines, reading tools, and editorial components.

Media & Images – 21 Blocks
Create engaging visual experiences with image galleries, sliders, video blocks, popups, media cards, before-and-after layouts, and other media-focused elements.

Marketing & Conversion – 53 Blocks
Create high-converting landing pages with call-to-action sections, pricing elements, countdowns, promotional banners, offer cards, social proof, lead-generation layouts, and conversion-focused components.

Business & Services – 39 Blocks
Build professional business websites with service sections, team members, testimonials, contact information, business hours, process sections, company information, and more.

Blog & Editorial – 50 Blocks
Enhance WordPress blogs and editorial websites with article headers, reading lists, reading time, FAQs, sources and references, expert roundups, research content, tutorials, related content, and other publishing-focused blocks.

Interactive – 21 Blocks
Add engaging experiences with quizzes, polls, flashcards, interactive steps, tabs, reveal effects, interactive cards, drawing tools, and other interactive elements.

Charts & Data – 39 Blocks
Present information visually using charts, graphs, tables, progress indicators, statistics, data visualizations, comparison tables, and other data-focused blocks.

Calculators & Tools – 29 Blocks
Add useful tools to your website with calculators and utilities such as ROI calculators, price calculators, discount calculators, loan calculators, compound interest calculators, date calculators, time zone converters, and more.

Effects & Animation – 60 Blocks
Create modern and engaging designs with animated text, hover effects, scroll animations, parallax effects, marquees, particle effects, gradient effects, glassmorphism, cursor effects, and other visual interactions.

Build More with the WordPress Block Editor

TemplateHouse Block Toolkit is designed around the native Gutenberg block editor, giving you more control without adding another page builder to your WordPress website.

Use individual blocks to create:

  • WordPress landing pages
  • Business and corporate websites
  • Agency websites
  • SaaS and startup websites
  • Portfolio websites
  • Blog and magazine websites
  • Affiliate and review websites
  • Marketing and sales pages
  • Product comparison pages
  • Documentation and knowledge bases
  • Online course and educational websites
  • Service-based business websites
  • Interactive tools and calculators
  • Data and statistics pages
  • Restaurant and local business websites

One Block Toolkit for Complete Websites

Instead of installing multiple WordPress block plugins for different features, TemplateHouse Block Toolkit brings a broad range of website-building components into one toolkit.

Create page structures, publish rich content, display business information, build marketing sections, present data, add interactive tools, and enhance your website with modern visual effects — all from the WordPress block editor.

Powerful and Flexible Block Controls

Each block is designed to give you practical customization options while keeping the editing experience simple.

Depending on the block, you can customize:

  • Typography
  • Colors
  • Backgrounds
  • Spacing
  • Borders
  • Border radius
  • Shadows
  • Alignment
  • Icons
  • Images
  • Buttons
  • Responsive layouts
  • Animation and hover effects
  • Desktop, tablet, and mobile settings

This makes it easy to match your blocks with your existing WordPress theme and brand style.

Built for Modern WordPress Websites

TemplateHouse Block Toolkit works with modern WordPress websites and is designed to complement both block themes and classic WordPress themes.

The plugin focuses on a clean editing experience, flexible design controls, responsive layouts, and performance-conscious frontend output.

Useful Blocks for SEO and Content Marketing

Create structured and useful content with blocks such as FAQ, Review Schema, Breadcrumbs, comparison tables, testimonials, article sections, reading tools, sources and references, and other editorial components.

These blocks can help you organize your content clearly and create better experiences for visitors while supporting your overall content marketing and SEO strategy.

Perfect for Freelancers and Agencies

TemplateHouse Block Toolkit is also useful for WordPress freelancers, designers, and agencies who build websites for clients.

With hundreds of reusable blocks available in one plugin, you can create landing pages, business websites, marketing pages, blogs, service websites, and custom content layouts faster without repeatedly developing common UI components from scratch.

Lightweight and Performance-Minded

TemplateHouse Block Toolkit is built with performance in mind. The plugin uses selective assets and focuses on keeping frontend output clean and efficient.

You can also enable or disable individual blocks to keep your WordPress editor focused on the features you actually need.

Key Features

  • 376+ Gutenberg blocks
  • 10 organized block categories
  • Native WordPress block editor integration
  • Responsive design controls
  • Advanced typography and styling options
  • Marketing and conversion blocks
  • Business and service blocks
  • Blog and editorial blocks
  • Charts and data visualization blocks
  • Calculators and interactive tools
  • Modern animation and effects
  • Image and media blocks
  • SEO-focused content blocks
  • Flexible responsive controls
  • Block manager for enabling or disabling blocks
  • Theme-friendly design
  • Suitable for freelancers and agencies
  • No dependency on Elementor or Divi

Create Without Limits

From a simple blog post to a complete business website, TemplateHouse Block Toolkit gives you the building blocks you need to create modern WordPress pages faster.

Build better pages. Add more functionality. Design with Gutenberg.

External services

This plugin does not phone home to TemplateHouse. It does not collect visitor data on its own. Some optional blocks connect to third-party services so they can show maps, weather, prices, videos, or share links. Those connections happen only when the matching block is on a page (and, where noted, only after a visitor clicks or an admin enters an API key). Each service may receive the visitor’s IP address and browser information as part of a normal HTTPS request.

Google Maps (Google Map block, Location Cards block)

Used to display an embedded map for an address the site editor enters, or to open a Google Maps search when a visitor clicks a location card.

When a Google Map block is shown, the visitor’s browser loads an iframe from Google Maps (maps.google.com or https://www.google.com/maps/embed/v1/place). The request includes the configured address/search query, zoom, map type, and — if the editor saved one — the site’s Google Maps Embed API key. Google may receive the visitor’s IP address, user agent, and similar browser data. Location Cards only send the address to Google when a visitor clicks to open Maps.

This service is provided by Google LLC: Google Maps/Google Earth Additional Terms of Service, Google Maps Platform Terms, Google Privacy Policy.

OpenWeatherMap (Weather Widget block)

Used to show current weather and an optional forecast for a city the editor configures, or for the visitor’s coordinates if “auto location” is enabled and the visitor allows geolocation.

When the weather block is shown and an OpenWeatherMap API key is saved in the block, the visitor’s browser requests https://api.openweathermap.org/data/2.5/weather and optionally /forecast. The request includes the API key, city name or latitude/longitude, units, and language. OpenWeatherMap may receive the visitor’s IP address and browser data. If auto location is off, no geolocation permission is requested.

This service is provided by OpenWeather Ltd.: Terms of use, Privacy policy.

CoinGecko (Stock Ticker block)

Used to display cryptocurrency market prices for coin IDs the editor configures (for example bitcoin, ethereum).

When the stock ticker block is shown, the visitor’s browser requests https://api.coingecko.com/api/v3/coins/markets with the selected coin IDs and currency. No visitor account data is sent. CoinGecko may receive the visitor’s IP address and browser data. Requests repeat on the refresh interval set in the block.

This service is provided by Gecko Labs Pte. Ltd. (CoinGecko): API Terms of Service, Privacy Policy.

WhatsApp (Social Share block, Phone Button block)

Used so a visitor can share the current page in WhatsApp, or start a WhatsApp chat with a number the editor configured.

No request is made to WhatsApp until the visitor clicks the share or chat button. The click opens https://api.whatsapp.com/send or https://wa.me/ with the page URL and optional pre-filled text, or the configured phone number. WhatsApp may then receive that content plus the visitor’s IP address and device data according to WhatsApp’s policies.

This service is provided by WhatsApp LLC: Terms of Service, Privacy Policy.

YouTube (video blocks: Video Popup, Playlist, Grid, Hero, Sticky Video, Video Testimonial, and similar)

Used only when an editor pastes a YouTube URL into a video block. The visitor’s browser then loads YouTube’s embed player and may load a thumbnail from https://img.youtube.com/. YouTube/Google may receive the video ID, the visitor’s IP address, cookies, and browser data.

This service is provided by Google LLC / YouTube: YouTube Terms of Service, Google Privacy Policy.

Vimeo (same video blocks, when a Vimeo URL is used)

Used only when an editor pastes a Vimeo URL. The visitor’s browser loads Vimeo’s embed player (https://player.vimeo.com/). Vimeo may receive the video ID, the visitor’s IP address, cookies, and browser data.

This service is provided by Vimeo.com, Inc.: Terms of Service, Privacy Policy.

Social share networks (Social Share block)

Share buttons open the selected network only after a visitor clicks. The click sends the current page URL and optional title/text as query parameters. No share request is made on page load.

  • X (Twitter): Terms, Privacy
  • Facebook: Terms, Privacy
  • LinkedIn: User Agreement, Privacy
  • Pinterest: Terms, Privacy
  • Telegram: Terms, Privacy
  • Reddit: User Agreement, Privacy

Google Fonts (optional, off by default)

Used only if a site administrator enables “Google Fonts” in Block Toolkit settings. Selected fonts are then requested from https://fonts.googleapis.com/ (and font files from https://fonts.gstatic.com/). That request may send the visitor’s IP address and browser data to Google. Leave the setting off to avoid any Google Fonts request.

This service is provided by Google LLC: Google Fonts Terms, Google Privacy Policy.

Chart.js (bundled)

Chart and loan-calculator blocks use Chart.js 4.4.3, MIT-licensed and bundled in assets/vendor/chart.js/. No CDN request is made. Upstream source: https://github.com/chartjs/Chart.js/tree/v4.4.3. License: https://github.com/chartjs/Chart.js/blob/v4.4.3/LICENSE.md

Natural Earth (World Map block)

Country outlines are bundled inside the plugin (public domain). No visitor request is sent to Natural Earth at runtime. Source: https://www.naturalearthdata.com/

Privacy

This plugin does not collect, store, or share personal data by default. It does not send usage analytics to TemplateHouse.

When you use an optional block that talks to a third party (maps, weather, prices, video embeds, share buttons, or Google Fonts), the visitor’s browser may send IP address and browser data to that provider. See External services above for what is sent, when, and links to each provider’s terms and privacy policy. Disclose those services in your own site privacy policy and obtain consent where required.

Third-Party Libraries

This plugin bundles Chart.js 4.4.3 (MIT) in assets/vendor/chart.js/ for chart and loan-calculator blocks. It does not include amCharts or other GPL-incompatible mapping libraries. The World Map block renders an SVG map with original JavaScript and locally bundled Natural Earth geography data (public domain).

Source Code

This plugin ships original, human-readable PHP, JavaScript, and CSS. It does not use npm, webpack, Babel, or another build step to generate block assets.

The files in /blocks (including each block’s index.js and frontend.js) and /assets are the source. They are not compiled, minified, or obfuscated. There is no separate src/ directory or generated bundle.

Chart.js 4.4.3 is a third-party MIT library bundled in assets/vendor/chart.js/ (UMD build plus LICENSE). Upstream source: https://github.com/chartjs/Chart.js/tree/v4.4.3

No build tools are required to review, modify, or fork the plugin. Edit the files in place.
sections.installation:
1. Upload the plugin files to the /wp-content/plugins/TemplateHouse Block Toolkit directory, or install the plugin through the WordPress plugins screen directly.
  2. Activate the plugin through the ‘Plugins’ screen in WordPress.
  3. Add TemplateHouse Block Toolkit blocks to your pages or posts using the WordPress block editor.
sections.faq:
What is TemplateHouse Block Toolkit?

TemplateHouse Block Toolkit is a collection of powerful and flexible blocks for the WordPress Block Editor. It provides a wide range of ready-to-use blocks to help you build modern and professional websites without writing custom code.

Does TemplateHouse Block Toolkit work with the WordPress Block Editor?

Yes. TemplateHouse Block Toolkit is designed specifically for the WordPress Block Editor and works directly with the native editing experience.

Do I need Elementor or another page builder?

No. TemplateHouse Block Toolkit works with the WordPress Block Editor, so you do not need Elementor, Divi, Beaver Builder, or another page builder to use the blocks.

Can I enable or disable individual blocks?

Yes. TemplateHouse Block Toolkit includes a block management interface that allows you to enable or disable individual blocks. This helps you keep only the blocks you need active on your website.

Can I disable all blocks at once?

Yes. You can use the “Enable All” and “Disable All” options in the plugin settings to quickly manage all available blocks.

What types of blocks are included?

TemplateHouse Block Toolkit includes blocks for different purposes, including structure, content, typography, media, marketing, business, blog, interactive elements, charts, calculators, effects, animations, and more.

Does TemplateHouse Block Toolkit include responsive controls?

Many TemplateHouse Block Toolkit blocks include responsive and layout controls to help you create designs that work well across desktop, tablet, and mobile devices.

Is TemplateHouse Block Toolkit suitable for beginners?

Yes. TemplateHouse Block Toolkit is designed to be easy to use with the WordPress Block Editor. You can build layouts and add advanced content without needing coding knowledge.

Can I use TemplateHouse Block Toolkit with any WordPress theme?

TemplateHouse Block Toolkit is designed to work with modern WordPress themes that support the WordPress Block Editor. Some block features may depend on the capabilities of your active theme.

Does TemplateHouse Block Toolkit slow down my website?

TemplateHouse Block Toolkit includes block management features that allow you to disable blocks you do not need. Disabling unused blocks can help reduce unnecessary assets and keep your website optimized.

Can I use TemplateHouse Block Toolkit on client websites?

Yes. You can use TemplateHouse Block Toolkit to build websites for yourself or your clients, subject to the plugin’s license terms.

Is TemplateHouse Block Toolkit free?

Yes. TemplateHouse Block Toolkit is available as a free WordPress plugin through the WordPress.org Plugin Directory.

Is coding knowledge required to use TemplateHouse Block Toolkit?

No. TemplateHouse Block Toolkit is designed to be used through the WordPress Block Editor. However, developers can also customize their websites using WordPress, CSS, JavaScript, and other development tools when needed.

Where can I get support?

For support, please use the support forum on WordPress.org or visit the plugin’s official website for documentation and additional information.

Does this plugin load Google Fonts or send data to third parties?

Google Fonts loading is turned off until a site administrator explicitly enables it in Block Toolkit settings. Some optional blocks connect to third-party services (maps, weather, stock prices, video embeds, or share links) only when you add that block and configure it. See the External services section below.

items.question: How does billing work?
items.answer: We bill monthly or annually depending on your chosen plan. You can upgrade, downgrade, or cancel at any time from your account settings.

default.content: Create a new React app using Create React App or Vite. Make sure you're using React 16.8 or higher to access Hooks.

default.title: Your First useState Hook
default.content: Replace your class component's `this.state` with the `useState` hook. Call `const [count, setCount] = useState(0)` at the top of your function component.
default.tip: Hooks must be called at the top level of your component — never inside loops or conditions.

default.title: Handle Side Effects with useEffect
default.content: Move your `componentDidMount` and `componentDidUpdate` logic into `useEffect`. Return a cleanup function to replicate `componentWillUnmount`.
default.tip: Pass an empty dependency array `[]` to run the effect only once on mount.

default.title: Build a Custom Hook
default.content: Extract reusable stateful logic into a function prefixed with `use`. Custom hooks let you share logic across components without changing the component hierarchy.
default.tip: Name custom hooks starting with `use` so React knows to apply the rules of Hooks.

default.title: Test Your Hooks
default.content: Use React Testing Library and `renderHook` from `@testing-library/react-hooks` to unit-test your custom hooks in isolation.

intro.default: In this lesson, you'll build a fully functional REST API using Express.js. We'll cover everything from project setup and route definition to data validation and database integration — all with real-world patterns you can use immediately.

default.heading: Setting Up the Project
default.content: Start by initializing a new Node.js project and installing Express. Run `npm init -y && npm install express` in your terminal. Create a file called `server.js` and require Express at the top.

default.heading: Defining Your First Route
default.content: Use `app.get()` to define a GET route. The callback receives a `req` (request) and `res` (response) object. Call `res.json()` to send JSON data back to the client.

default.heading: Pro Tip: Use nodemon During Development
default.content: Install nodemon as a dev dependency (`npm install -D nodemon`) and add a `dev` script to your package.json: `"dev": "nodemon server.js"`. This automatically restarts your server on file changes.

default.heading: Handling POST Requests & Body Parsing
default.content: For POST and PUT routes, you need to parse the request body. Add `app.use(express.json())` before your routes. Access the parsed body via `req.body`.
